s: Uniform mTLS, retries, timeouts, and telemetry for service-to-service calls - implemented as sidecar proxies so apps stay clean.
w: Each pod gets a sidecar proxy; all outbound/inbound traffic detours through it. The mesh control plane distributes certificates (mTLS identity), retry budgets, circuit-breaker settings, and collects L7 metrics/traces centrally. Policy is declared once, enforced everywhere regardless of language.
use: 50+ polyglot microservices needing consistent security and reliability defaults
Zero-trust networks: every hop mutually authenticated
Progressive delivery: mesh-level traffic splitting for canaries
Unified golden metrics (success rate, p99 per service-pair) without instrumenting each codebase
avoid: Latency-critical tight loops where sidecar hops hurt p99
Teams lacking platform engineering capacity to operate control planes

size.rps_per_instance: Sidecars add ~0.5-2ms and ~50-100MB RAM per pod

pat.d: The mesh's unit of deployment - platform features ride beside the app container.
Mesh enforces outlier ejection so one bad upstream doesn't cascade.

pits: Upgrade storms - mesh versions must roll across every pod; plan canary node pools
Debugging opacity - failures move from app code into proxy config; invest in mesh dashboards early
tips: Name the tradeoff: uniform platform goodness vs operational weight; mention ambient/eBPF meshes reducing sidecar tax
